statement: In the calculation $1 + 2 + 3 - 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 - 8 + \dots + 21 + 22 + 23 - 24$, every fourth number is subtracted and all the others are added. What is the result?

choices.misconception: I only added up the numbers that are subtracted, 4 + 8 + ... + 24.
I grouped the numbers in fours, but I only made five groups instead of six.
I added all the numbers to get 300 and then took away the multiples of 4 only once.
I added all the numbers from 1 to 24 and ignored the minus signs.

hints: Look at the numbers in groups of four.
Group the terms in fours, each group ending with a subtracted number. Work out what each group is worth and look for a pattern in those values, then add them up.
The groups give 1 + 2 + 3 - 4 = 2, 5 + 6 + 7 - 8 = 10, 9 + 10 + 11 - 12 = 18, and so on. There are six groups, worth 2, 10, 18, 26, 34 and 42.

solutions.reliable: Group the terms in fours: (1 + 2 + 3 - 4) + (5 + 6 + 7 - 8) + ... + (21 + 22 + 23 - 24). The groups are worth 2, 10, 18, 26, 34 and 42, six groups going up by 8. Pair them from the outside in: 2 + 42 = 10 + 34 = 18 + 26 = 44, so the sum is 3 × 44 = 132. Second method: all numbers from 1 to 24 add to 300, and the multiples of 4 add to 4 + 8 + ... + 24 = 84. Each multiple of 4 is subtracted instead of added, which takes away twice its value: 300 - 2 × 84 = 132. The transferable idea: group terms so the pattern repeats, and check by a second grouping.
solutions.elegant: Every subtracted number is counted with the wrong sign, so start from the full total and take each of them away twice: 300 - 2 × 84 = 132.

whyOnTest: Clever regrouping: pairing or tripling terms turns a long sum into a short pattern you can add in your head.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
